main_body: A flat tiling pattern of stone bricks in running bond, seen face-on as a wall face
top_band: none. This is a terrain wall-face tile, not a standing object, so it has no top surface to read. Each brick has a light top and left bevel line 1px wide, which is a bevel and not a top plane.
evidence: The candidate is a seamless terrain tile of a brick wall face, which is a vertical surface drawn flat by design. Bricks have a 1px light bevel and dark mortar joints, and no standing volume is claimed. The 3/4 top-plus-front contract for standing objects does not apply to terrain, and nothing in the tile is a mis-drawn standing object. Passed on that basis.

style.evidence: The tile uses about 5 tones: pale tan bevel, mid taupe brick, a lighter speckle, dark mortar and a deeper mortar shadow. The mortar is a tinted dark brown-grey, not pure black. Each brick interior is a large flat mid-tone block of roughly 12x6 px with only 2-3 sparse speckle dots, so these are flat fills. The paving reference carries per-stone shading, many tones and varied cobble grain, and each of its tiles is richer. The brick tile repeats a single flat brick with a bevel, so it is thinner and more uniform than the reference.
